args.summary: 35M with ulcerative colitis on mesalazine. Two weeks after a respiratory infection he developed progressive NYHA III dyspnoea, leg oedema and abdominal pain. HR 42/min. ECG shows no P waves and a narrow-QRS escape rhythm at 42/min. NT-proBNP 432 and hs-TnT 31 are both raised. TTE: LV systolic function preserved, LA and RV dilated, RV function impaired, severe TR, sPAP 58 mmHg. D-dimer 2.94, but CTPA shows no PE; it shows RV dilatation, bilateral pleural effusions and contrast reflux into the hepatic veins (congestive hepatopathy likely explains the abdominal pain). Cardiac MRI: left atrial LGE, borderline T1/T2 oedema, no substantial ventricular scar. Overall picture: suspected atrial standstill from post-viral (or mesalazine-related) atrial myocarditis, with loss of atrial contraction, bradycardia and right-sided congestive heart failure.
working_diagnoses: Atrial standstill due to isolated atrial myocarditis (post-viral), causing a junctional escape rhythm and right heart failure
Cardiac sarcoidosis or another infiltrative/autoimmune myocarditis (IBD-associated)
Hyperkalaemia or drug-induced loss of P waves (potassium not yet reported)
Genetic atrial cardiomyopathy (e.g., SCN5A-related) causing atrial standstill
next_actions: Continuous telemetry, with transcutaneous or temporary transvenous pacing ready if he becomes haemodynamically unstable
Check potassium and renal function before diuresis
Start IV loop diuretic for right-sided congestion
Electrophysiology study to confirm atrial electrical silence, then plan a permanent pacemaker (VVI/ventricular pacing)
Consider stopping mesalazine and giving anticoagulation because of atrial standstill and thromboembolic risk

args.rationale: 35-year-old man with symptomatic bradycardia at 42/min (physical_exam_004). ECG shows no P waves and a narrow-QRS escape rhythm (ecg_005). The picture is consistent with atrial standstill from post-viral atrial myocarditis: cardiac MRI shows left atrial LGE with borderline oedema (imaging_014), and troponin is raised (lab_007). He also has right heart failure: RV dysfunction, severe TR and sPAP 58 mmHg on echo (ecg_009), bilateral pleural effusions and hepatic venous congestion on CTPA (imaging_010), and a raised NT-proBNP (lab_006). An escape rhythm can fail, so he needs a monitored bed with pacing immediately available until a permanent pacemaker is implanted. Potassium and renal function have not been reported; they must be checked before hyperkalaemia or drug causes are ruled out and while he is on diuretics.
args.followup_or_handoff: Hand over to cardiology/CCU and electrophysiology. Keep transcutaneous pacing pads on, with temporary transvenous pacing if the escape rhythm becomes unstable. Order stat potassium, magnesium, creatinine and TSH. Continue IV furosemide 40 mg twice daily with daily weights, fluid balance and electrolytes. The EP study to confirm atrial electrical silence and permanent pacemaker implantation (VVI(R) unless atrial capture is shown) are ordered. Discuss anticoagulation given atrial standstill and thromboembolic risk. Review mesalazine with gastroenterology as a possible cause of myocarditis. Arrange genetic and sarcoidosis work-up if clinically indicated, and repeat cardiac MRI and echo on follow-up.
